issues.description: Neither the Japanese quoted statement nor って establishes a female speaker. The fixed text has no speaker labels, and ミオ、 also leaves the vocative/subject interpretation open. Translation and utterance meaning both assert gender without qualification.
issues.suggestedDirection: Preserve the quote with an unspecified reporting subject and mark unresolved references in each affected field.

issues.description: The affected translation and utterance meaning retain the literal token but do not identify it as unclear. The full damaged quote is also promoted to a reusable source form without a local caveat. This fails the fixed uncertainty gate. The reliable surrounding って何？ construction is valid to teach; the failure does not mean the output invented a meaning for 悪いない.
issues.suggestedDirection: Mark the damaged token as unresolved in each affected rendering; teach only reliable surrounding material and avoid promoting the unclear token as a reusable source target.

issues.description: The slot says to use the verb te-form, which already ends in て or で, then appends another てた. 話して + てた produces 話しててた instead of the source 話してた; 読んで + てた likewise fails. A complete te-form slot does not itself contain the auxiliary い to delete. The point explanation correctly reconstructs 話していた, and the concrete example is correct, but they do not repair the contradictory reusable template.
issues.suggestedDirection: Use the full underlying [動詞て形]いた and explain deletion of only い, or the resulting [動詞て形]た; check both て- and で-ending substitutions.

boundary: AI source/editorial screening against this fixed text-only rubric. Coverage failure is not by itself a language error. No audio, native-speaker certification, learning-effect measurement or actual Chrome acceptance.
